# Audio AI

The client half of Field Audio: a separate HTTP/WebSocket service that runs generative and analysis models over audio, and the typed vocabulary a box talks to it in. Nothing here loads a model or does inference in the JVM — a box builds a `ModelOperation`, submits it through `FieldAudioClient`, and gets back a job it can poll or watch; the results are immutable server-side *assets* referenced by id, which is why the protocol types carry representation ids rather than samples. Every call is asynchronous and completes off Field's runloop and off the audio callback, so nothing here may be `.get()`-ed from a box's frame. The rest of the category is what you do with a result inside a box: the candidate browser, the EnCodec reconstruction microscope, the beat/pitch analysis viewer and the job monitor, each of them one function returning a self-contained HTML fragment for `display(…)`. Start from `Protocol.kt` for the vocabulary and `FieldAudioClient.kt` for the verbs; [Field Audio service reference](../field_audio_service_reference.md) is the service-side contract the types mirror.

## AnalysisOperations.kt { #analysisoperations-kt }

Typed constructors for model-free musical analysis and learned speech representations.

Each one is a [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation) factory and nothing more — it validates its arguments here in the
JVM, names the backend that serves it, and packs the parameters into the snake_case keys that
backend expects. Submitting it, waiting for it and drawing it are `FieldAudioClient`'s job.

Every constructor asks for a single candidate, because an analysis of a fixed window with fixed parameters
has one answer; the seed family in `styleCandidates` has no counterpart here. All three also
produce an `.npz` of full-resolution arrays plus, for a drawing, a downsampled
[`AnalysisPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysispreview) — see `analysisVisualizationHtml`.

Which to reach for: `multiScaleBeatAnalysis` when you want *when*, and at several time scales at
once, because a tempo estimate is only meaningful relative to a window length;
`monophonicPitchAnalysis` when you know there is one voice and want a continuous F0 with a voiced
probability; `polyphonicPitchAnalysis` when there are chords and you want discrete note events
(and MIDI) rather than a curve.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/AnalysisOperations.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/AnalysisOperations/)

**Used in:** [Multi-instrument transcription with MuScriptor](../audio_ai_muscriptor.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md), [Beat and pitch analysis](../audio_ai_analysis.md)

## AnalysisVisualization.kt { #analysisvisualization-kt }

Analysis viewers and dashboards for beat, pitch, and note results, with zoom, pan, and a shared time cursor.

[`analysisVisualizationHtml`](audio-ai.md#analysisvisualization-kt--analysisvisualizationhtml) turns an [`AnalysisResult`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysisresult) into a zoomable interactive display; the
browser decides which of the three layouts to draw from [`AnalysisPreview.operation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt--analysispreview--operation): onset
strength and multi-scale tempo for a beat analysis, pYIN frequency and voicing probability for
a monophonic pitch analysis, or a Basic Pitch piano roll with activation curves for a
polyphonic one. [`analysisPreviewVisualizationHtml`](audio-ai.md#analysisvisualization-kt--analysispreviewvisualizationhtml) takes an already-fetched [`AnalysisPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysispreview)
and works without any service round trip.

Dashboard variants ([`analysisDashboardHtml`](audio-ai.md#analysisvisualization-kt--analysisdashboardhtml), [`analysisPreviewDashboardHtml`](audio-ai.md#analysisvisualization-kt--analysispreviewdashboardhtml)) stack panels with
a synchronized cursor, making beat/pYIN/Basic Pitch disagreements inspectable side by side.
All panels support wheel zoom, drag pan, hover inspection, and click-to-seek, synchronized
across panels that share a `syncGroup`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/AnalysisVisualization.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/AnalysisVisualization/)

**Used in:** [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md), [Multi-instrument transcription with MuScriptor](../audio_ai_muscriptor.md)

## AudioAssetVisualization.kt { #audioassetvisualization-kt }

The one-line bridge from a Field Audio [`AssetRepresentation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetrepresentation) to Field's general-purpose waveform
player.

It exists so that playing a service asset needs no URL arithmetic: the extension resolves the
binary path and the server-side waveform endpoint against the same-origin `/field-audio` prefix
and hands both to `AudioVisualizer`, which then fetches only the envelope of whatever window the
user is looking at.

## CandidateBoard.kt { #candidateboard-kt }

The candidate board: the instrument for choosing between the alternatives a generation produced.

One function, one HTML fragment, three things a listener actually needs — a player per candidate,
the source-into-candidate splice preview beside it so a take can be judged *in place* rather than
in isolation, and a rating, selection flag and note that are written straight back to the service.
The provenance line under each player states the sample rates and the conversion, because whether
you are hearing the model or a resampler is not a detail.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/CandidateBoard.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/CandidateBoard/)

## CodecVisualization.kt { #codecvisualization-kt }

The EnCodec reconstruction microscope: what a neural codec kept, what it threw away, and what it
wrote down in between.

A codec round trip is three things that have to be looked at together — the audio in, the discrete
tokens, the audio out — and this file is the rendering half of that view. It is
browser-free below the top layer: the spectrograms, the waveform and the token map are drawn into
PNG bytes on the JVM, so the same code produces a live box output, a test assertion and the
committed picture on [the EnCodec microscope page](../audio_ai_codec.md).

Everything here needs the bytes locally, which is what `FieldAudioClient.codecVisualizationHtml`
is for — it downloads the three representations off Field's runloop and then renders.

## CorpusClip.kt { #corpusclip-kt }

Turns a window of a recording in the Field audio corpus into a box that plays it.

[`corpusClip`](audio-ai.md#corpusclip-kt--corpusclip) fetches a recording from the Field audio service, caches its WAV, and cuts the
requested window into a [`CorpusClip`](audio-ai.md#corpusclip-kt-corpusclip), whose [`CorpusClip.sampler`](audio-ai.md#corpusclip-kt--corpusclip--sampler) plays it. The rest of the file
places a neighbour found by the corpus microscope ([`corpusMicroscopeHtml`](audio-ai.md#corpusmicroscope-kt--corpusmicroscopehtml)) as a box of its own:
[`corpusNeighbourName`](audio-ai.md#corpusclip-kt--corpusneighbourname) and [`corpusNeighbourCode`](audio-ai.md#corpusclip-kt--corpusneighbourcode) give the box its name and its `code`, and
[`placeCorpusNeighbour`](audio-ai.md#corpusclip-kt--placecorpusneighbour) creates it beside an existing box.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/CorpusClip.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/CorpusClip/)

## CorpusMicroscope.kt { #corpusmicroscope-kt }

The audition surface for a corpus nearest-neighbour query: the query window and every window
the search returned, as players on one shared relative timeline.

[`corpusMicroscopeHtml`](audio-ai.md#corpusmicroscope-kt--corpusmicroscopehtml) turns the [`CorpusPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-corpuspreview) an `analysis.find_neighbours` job leaves behind
into a single self-contained section of HTML, and it refuses a preview from any other operation.
Nothing in it reads audio: each [`AssetRepresentation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetrepresentation) in the preview becomes a media URL and a
waveform URL handed to [`AudioVisualizer`](visualization.md#audiovisualizer-kt-audiovisualizer), which does the fetching, the drawing and the
shared-cursor arithmetic.

A card's header prints two readings of the same number. One is the raw [`CorpusNeighbour`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-corpusneighbour)
distance; the other is a percentage that maps distance 0 to 100% and saturates at 2, so a
neighbour further away than that reads as no similarity at all. The per-group bars apply the
same mapping to each entry of `groupDistances` and keep the raw distance in the tooltip, so a
bar and the header can be read against each other. The weights above the grid are taken from
the preview, which means they arrive with the result rather than from the
[`CorpusDistanceWeights`](audio-ai.md#corpusoperations-kt-corpusdistanceweights) the query was written with.

The footer carries what the players cannot. A retrieved window is a stretch of some other
recording, so the card keeps its absolute start and end, its scale in seconds, and whether
[`CorpusSegment`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-corpussegment) records a previous and a next window. A neighbour that sits at the very
beginning or the very end of its recording shows up there.

## CorpusOperations.kt { #corpusoperations-kt }

Multi-scale corpus operations: segment a source into overlapping windows, embed each window
with grouped audio descriptors, and retrieve neighbours by weighted distance.

The three operations form a pipeline that runs server-side. [`segmentCorpus`](audio-ai.md#corpusoperations-kt--segmentcorpus) enumerates
deterministic time windows at several scales without computing any descriptors. [`embedCorpus`](audio-ai.md#corpusoperations-kt--embedcorpus)
computes and persists the five grouped descriptor families (harmony, pitch, texture, rhythm,
dynamics) for every window. [`findCorpusNeighbours`](audio-ai.md#corpusoperations-kt--findcorpusneighbours) retrieves the closest embedded windows
to a query using [`CorpusDistanceWeights`](audio-ai.md#corpusoperations-kt-corpusdistanceweights), which controls how much each group contributes to
the distance. All three produce a [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation) that [`FieldAudioClient.submit`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt--fieldaudioclient--submit) executes.

## FieldAudioClient.kt { #fieldaudioclient-kt }

The verbs of Field Audio: one client object whose every method is a request to the model
service, plus the typed constructors for the two operations that ship with real controls.

The protocol types — [`AssetRegion`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetregion), [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation), [`JobRecord`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobrecord) and the rest — are the
vocabulary; this is what you can *do* with it. The shape to hold on to is that nothing here
blocks and nothing here runs a model in the JVM: a call returns
a `CompletableFuture` that completes on the client's own executor, and the model work happens in
a Python worker that may take minutes. Composing futures (`thenCompose`, `thenAccept`) is
therefore the only correct way to use this from a box — a `.get()` on Field's runloop freezes
the editor for as long as the model takes.

Argument validation happens here, in the JVM, before anything is sent: `require` failures name
the constraint. Everything the service rejects instead arrives as a [`FieldAudioException`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudioexception)
carrying the service's own [`StructuredError`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-structurederror), and a job that fails after being accepted arrives
as a [`FieldAudioJobException`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudiojobexception) from one of the `await…` helpers.

## FieldPersistence.kt { #fieldpersistence-kt }

How a Field document remembers audio work: ids and judgements in a box property, and not one
sample of audio.

The rule this file enforces is that Python is a worker and Field is the authority. The service
owns immutable, content-addressed assets; the document owns which of them it refers to and what
you thought of them. That is why saved state is a [`FieldAudioProjectState`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-fieldaudioprojectstate) of ids rather than
audio, and why reopening a document and re-fetching those ids gets the same bytes back.

## GestureBoard.kt { #gestureboard-kt }

Temporal sketches for source-conditioned generation, with prompt regions, onset events,
and parameter curves that together express a generation intent.

Build a [`GestureBoard`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-gestureboard) with the `gestureBoard{}` DSL and pass it to [`gestureCandidates`](audio-ai.md#gestureboard-kt--gesturecandidates) to
produce a multi-seed [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation). Prompt regions are compiled into the model's global text
condition; onset events and parameter curves are evaluative: the service scores each generated
candidate against them rather than passing them as native model controls.

[`compileGestureBoard`](audio-ai.md#gestureboard-kt--compilegestureboard) previews the protocol locally and returns a [`GestureCompilation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-gesturecompilation) that lists
how each board element is wired to the backend. Example:

    val board = gestureBoard(8.0, "acoustic guitar, warm") {
        prompt(0.0, 4.0, "sparse, arpeggiated")
        event(3.5, "accent")
        curve("energy", GestureCurveKind.ACTIVITY) {
            point(0.0, 0.2); point(4.0, 0.8); point(8.0, 0.3)
        }
    }
    val operation = gestureCandidates(source, board, seeds = 0L until 4L)

Like an event, a curve is measured against the generated waveform rather than sent as a model control, and the pinned contract has four kinds to measure against: density, activity, register and brightness. |

## GestureBoardVisualization.kt { #gestureboardvisualization-kt }

A gesture board drawn as a picture of itself: prompt regions, onset events and parameter curves
on one timeline, each mark labelled with how far into the model it reaches.

[`gestureBoardHtml`](audio-ai.md#gestureboardvisualization-kt--gestureboardhtml) renders a [`GestureBoard`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-gestureboard) as a single self-contained section, with inline
styles, one SVG and a few lines of script for the hover cursor. There is no asset to fetch and
no library to install. Every rule and the script are scoped to an id derived from the board's
hash, so one document can show several boards at once. Prompt regions become blocks on the
prompt lane, events become dashed needles at their marked time, and each curve gets a lane of
its own coloured by its [`GestureCurveKind`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-gesturecurvekind).

The chips above the timeline are the bindings of a [`GestureCompilation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-gesturecompilation), and they separate a
mark the backend is conditioned on from a mark it is only scored against. By default the
compilation is the local [`compileGestureBoard`](audio-ai.md#gestureboard-kt--compilegestureboard) preview of the service's version-1 contract
rather than a record of what some particular job sent, and the effective prompt printed beside
the chips is the time-worded text that preview produces.

Passing a [`CandidateSet`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-candidateset) adds a ranking strip under the chips: a row per candidate, ordered by
gesture score where the service returned one and by the candidate's own score otherwise, with a
bar for each evaluated lane. A board is validated before anything is drawn, so a sketch the
service would reject fails here rather than being rendered.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/GestureBoardVisualization.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/GestureBoardVisualization/)

## JobMonitor.kt { #jobmonitor-kt }

The job monitor: the service's own live view of every durable job, embedded in a box output.

It is an `<iframe>` rather than a Kotlin-rendered table, because the page is served by the
same service that owns the jobs, so it cannot disagree with them, and it needs no polling code on
the Field side. Same-origin through the `/field-audio` prefix, so nothing here reaches across
origins.

## MusicTranscription.kt { #musictranscription-kt }

Typed decoder for the versioned note document a multi-instrument transcription job leaves behind.

`musicTranscriptionAnalysis` in `AnalysisOperations.kt` builds the request, and three accessors
beside it locate what came back: performance MIDI, optional beat-quantized MIDI, and the
MessagePack event document. This file reads the last of those.
`decodeMusicTranscriptionMessagePack` turns its bytes into a [`MusicTranscription`](audio-ai.md#musictranscription-kt-musictranscription), and
`FieldAudioClient.musicTranscription` is the one-call path from a finished [`AnalysisResult`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysisresult).

MessagePack rather than JSON keeps the note times binary, so an onset reaches the JVM as the
float64 the worker wrote. The decoder rejects a payload whose `format` is not
`field.audio.music-transcription.v1`, rejects trailing data after the root map, and range-checks
every note: non-negative onset, offset at or after onset, MIDI pitch inside 0..127. A malformed
artifact fails at the decode rather than at the first drawing that reads it.

Most of the document is optional. `MusicTranscription.beatGrid` is null when the artifact carries
no `beat_grid` or a nil one, and inside a grid `beatsPerBar`, `onsetDelaySeconds` and
`beatSubdivision` are each independently absent. The four provenance fields come from the
artifact's `metadata` map and are null when the worker recorded nothing there. `instrument` is a
string naming one of the worker's own instrument groups, which is a model's hypothesis about a
mixed recording and not a reading of what played it. See
[Multi-instrument transcription with MuScriptor](../audio_ai_muscriptor.md) for how far that has
been checked against a known source.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/MusicTranscription.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/MusicTranscription/)

## NpyIntTensor.kt { #npyinttensor-kt }

A dependency-free reader for the integer NPY tensors the audio service emits — the codec token
grids, in practice.

`numpy.kt` already reads `.npy` and `.npz` generally; this is the narrow, self-checking version
for the one shape that matters here (codebooks × frames of small integers), so the codec views
can index tokens by codebook and frame without a general tensor type in between. It refuses what
it cannot represent, rather than guessing: Fortran order, an unsupported dtype and a
multi-item batch are all errors with a message.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/NpyIntTensor.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/NpyIntTensor/)

## Protocol.kt { #protocol-kt }

The wire vocabulary of Field Audio — one Kotlin type per JSON object in the pinned service
contract, and nothing else.

Field Audio runs models out of process: a long-lived Python service owns inference, and a box
talks to it over HTTP and one WebSocket through [`FieldAudioClient`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudioclient). These are the values that
cross that boundary. Every `SerialName` here is the snake_case name the service uses, and the
committed, model-free snapshot of the same contract is published as
[the Field Audio service reference](../field_audio_service_reference.md) — if the two disagree,
the service is right and this file is stale.

### Three facts that explain the shapes

- **Results are assets, not samples.** Everything the service produces is written once, named by
  the SHA-256 of its bytes (`sha256:` followed by 64 hex digits) and referred to afterwards by
  id. That is why a result type carries an [`AssetRepresentation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetrepresentation) rather than a `FloatArray`: the
  audio is still on the service, and `FieldAudioClient.download` is how bytes reach the JVM.
- **Work is a job, not a call.** Submitting an operation returns a [`JobAccepted`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobaccepted) immediately;
  the outcome arrives later as a [`JobRecord`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobrecord) you poll or a stream of [`ProgressEvent`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-progressevent)s you watch.
- **Identical requests are not repeated.** The service hashes the request (ignoring
  [`ModelOperation.forceRegenerate`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt--modeloperation--forceregenerate)) into [`JobRecord.requestHash`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt--jobrecord--requesthash) and returns the stored result
  when it has seen that hash before, with `cacheHit = true` and a job that is already complete.

### Times, ids and timestamps

All times and durations are **seconds** as `Double` unless the property name says otherwise.
`createdAt`, `updatedAt` and [`ProgressEvent.at`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt--progressevent--at) are ISO-8601 UTC timestamp *strings*, kept as
text because nothing in Field parses them and a string round-trips through project persistence
unchanged. Ids are opaque and prefixed by kind: `sha256:` for assets, `rep_` for
representations, `job_`, `op_`, `cset_`, `codec_` and `analysis_` for the rest.

The client decodes with `ignoreUnknownKeys`, so a newer service that adds a field will not break
an older Field; the reverse is not true, because the service rejects unknown fields it is sent.

## RenderedAudioAnalysis.kt { #renderedaudioanalysis-kt }

The render-to-analysis pipeline: render Field synthesis to a WAV, upload it once, and fan out durable analysis jobs.

[`RenderedAudioFile`](audio-ai.md#renderedaudioanalysis-kt-renderedaudiofile) is a WAV produced by Field code, tagged with a generator name and a
provenance map that identify what produced the bytes. Six render functions cover the synthesis
systems: `renderPatWav` (Pat rhythmic patterns), `renderDirtWav` (Pat through the Dirt sample
library), `renderDoughWav` and `renderDoughStereoWav` (Dough signal graphs), `renderFaustWav`
and `renderFaustWavAsync` (Faust programs), and `recordSonicPiWav` (real-time Sonic Pi capture).

[`analyzeRenderedAudio`](audio-ai.md#renderedaudioanalysis-kt--analyzerenderedaudio) uploads the WAV once, submits a fan-out of analysis jobs (beats,
monophonic pitch, and polyphonic pitch by default), watches progress over WebSocket, and
completes with a [`RenderedAudioAnalysis`](audio-ai.md#renderedaudioanalysis-kt-renderedaudioanalysis). The fan-out is all-or-nothing: a failed leg abandons
the others rather than returning a partial result. [`RenderedAudioAnalysis.visualizationHtml`](audio-ai.md#renderedaudioanalysis-kt--renderedaudioanalysis--visualizationhtml)
renders the waveform and all analysis lanes on a shared, bidirectional time cursor.

    val wav = renderPatWav(tmp, pattern, cycles = 4, cps = 1.5)
    val analysis = client.analyzeRenderedAudio(wav).get()
    display(analysis.visualizationHtml())

## SpectralEmbeddingProjection.kt { #spectralembeddingprojection-kt }

Spectral embedding: decode, pool, and project the short-time spectral frames stored in an analysis artifact.

A spectral analysis job writes a binary MessagePack artifact.
[`decodeSpectralEmbeddingMessagePack`](audio-ai.md#spectralembeddingprojection-kt--decodespectralembeddingmessagepack) reads it into a [`SpectralEmbeddingFrames`](audio-ai.md#spectralembeddingprojection-kt-spectralembeddingframes) value containing
mel distributions, log-mel spectrograms, and MFCC vectors, optionally bounded to a time window,
temporally pooled, and sampled to a target frame count. Call `.mds()` or `.tsne()` on the
result to get a [`SpectralEmbeddingProjection`](audio-ai.md#spectralembeddingprojection-kt-spectralembeddingprojection) with exact frame times, then pass it to
`withSpectralProjection` to attach the axes to an `AnalysisPreview` as named time series.

Five distance metrics are available via [`SpectralEmbeddingDistance`](audio-ai.md#spectralembeddingprojection-kt-spectralembeddingdistance). The default, mel Wasserstein,
treats each frame as a probability distribution over perceptual mel-bin positions and computes
earth-mover distance. The other four apply cosine or Euclidean distance to log-mel or MFCC
vectors directly. Both projection methods delegate to Smile via the `smileMds` and `smileTsne`
families.

Temporal pooling and hop length are independent: overlapping perceptual windows can still sample
at display rate. Sampling to `maxFrames` happens after pooling and retains time order. Example:

    val frames = client.spectralEmbeddingFrames(result).get()
    val projection = frames.mds()
    val preview = preview.withSpectralProjection(projection)

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/audio/ai/SpectralEmbeddingProjection.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/audio/ai/SpectralEmbeddingProjection/)

**Used in:** [Short-time spectral spaces](../audio_ai_spectral_embeddings.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md)

## SpeechEmbeddingMds.kt { #speechembeddingmds-kt }

Speech embedding: decode, pool, and project the learned speech frames stored in an analysis artifact.

`speechEmbeddingAnalysis` submits the `analysis.embed_speech` job, and the worker keeps two
things: the full float16 frame tensor, and its own four-axis MDS preview over cosine distance.
This file is the second route to a picture. `decodeSpeechEmbeddingMessagePack` reads the tensor
into a [`SpeechEmbeddingFrames`](audio-ai.md#speechembeddingmds-kt-speechembeddingframes) bounded to a time window, then `.mds()` or `.tsne()` fits the
projection in Field through Smile's `smileMds` and `smileTsne`. Changing the range, the pooling,
the distance, the dimension count, the perplexity or the seed re-fits locally and never re-runs
the speech model.

The payload stores float64 times and float16 vectors as little-endian MessagePack binary fields,
and a private half-float expansion reads them, so nothing here needs JVM float16 support. The
decoder rejects any `format` other than `field.audio.speech-embedding.v1`, and any dtype pair
other than those two.

Pooling and hop are independent. `poolMillis` is the width of a centred mean window and
`hopMillis` is the spacing between the vectors that come out of it. Both round to the frame rate
recorded in the payload, and omitting them preserves the model's own frames one for one. Pooling
runs as a rolling sum, so a window covering many source rows costs one pass over the range
instead of one pass per output row, and `maxFrames` sampling happens after pooling and keeps time
order.

    client.speechEmbeddingSmileTsnePreview(result).thenAccept { preview ->
        display("speech space", speechEmbeddingPreviewVisualizationHtml(preview))
    }

`withSpeechMds` and `withSpeechTsne` replace a preview's projection axes with the locally fitted
ones and stamp the owner, library and method into both the series metadata and the preview's
analysis object, which is how a Field-fitted view is told apart from the worker's cached one on
the page. Both require at least four dimensions, because
`speechEmbeddingPreviewVisualizationHtml` draws axes 0/1 and 2/3 as two phase portraits.

Every projection result carries the frame times and source frame indices it was fitted from
alongside the backend, model id, model revision and WavLM layer, so a trajectory on screen can be
traced back to the rows and the checkpoint behind it. The coordinates themselves are
navigational: axis numbering is specific to one fit, and comparing coordinate 0 between two
backends or two independently fitted recordings has no meaning. Use the stored vectors for that.
See [Speech-reactive learned spaces](../audio_ai_speech_embeddings.md).

## SpeechEmbeddingVisualization.kt { #speechembeddingvisualization-kt }

Phase portrait renderers for speech and spectral embedding spaces, synchronized with a shared audio cursor.

Two kinds of space are supported. Speech embeddings come from learned models such as WavLM and
use voice activity as the opacity modulator. Spectral embeddings come from
[`SpectralEmbeddingProjection`](audio-ai.md#spectralembeddingprojection-kt-spectralembeddingprojection) and use spectral flux instead. Both draw two phase portraits
(axes 0/1 and 2/3) above an activity strip, with hover audition and click-to-seek wired into
the same `field-time-*` event bus as the audio player.

Each kind has three entry points: a single-panel live variant that fetches from an
[`AnalysisResult`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysisresult), a single-panel preview variant that works from a cached [`AnalysisPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysispreview),
and a multi-panel dashboard that stacks several panels with a shared cursor. The spectral
variants accept the MDS or t-SNE preview that `withSpectralProjection` attaches to an
[`AnalysisPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysispreview).

## TrackedAnalysis.kt { #trackedanalysis-kt }

One explicit analysis request, followed from submission to durable result.

[`FieldAudioClient`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudioclient) has four separate verbs for the stages of that, each returning its own future:
`submit`, `watch`, `awaitAnalysis` and `inspect`. [`trackAnalysis`](audio-ai.md#trackedanalysis-kt--trackanalysis) composes them into a single
future owned by the calling run, with a callback at each stage, which is what a box asking one
question of the service usually wants. Ownership divides along the way: the subscription and the
polling belong to the run and are released when it stops, while the job belongs to the service and
goes on, since another client may be waiting on the same result.

## UnderfitOperations.kt { #underfitoperations-kt }

Request builder for source-conditioned Stable Audio 3 generation, with LoRAs named by digest.

`underfitCandidates` is a [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation) factory and nothing more: it validates its arguments
here in the JVM, names `underfit.stable_audio_3` as the backend, and packs everything into the
snake_case keys that backend expects. Submitting it, waiting on it and auditioning the candidate
board are `FieldAudioClient`'s job. Stable Audio 3 and Underfit themselves stay in an optional
Python worker, so the Kotlin here knows a wire operation name and a parameter vocabulary rather
than a model.

The source [`AssetRegion`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetregion) is sent as init audio, and `initNoiseLevel` on
[`UnderfitGenerationControls`](audio-ai.md#underfitoperations-kt-underfitgenerationcontrols) sets how far generation may travel from it. One candidate is
requested per seed, so the default `0L until 8L` asks for eight. [`UnderfitOperation`](audio-ai.md#underfitoperations-kt-underfitoperation) chooses
between the `generate.style` and `generate.variations` wire operations, and [`UnderfitModel`](audio-ai.md#underfitoperations-kt-underfitmodel)
carries the duration ceiling of each checkpoint pack, which `underfitCandidates` checks
`durationSeconds` against before building anything.

A LoRA is identified by a path relative to the worker's configured LoRA root plus the lowercase
SHA-256 of its `.safetensors` bytes, and both travel with the request. So a request names one
exact set of weights rather than a filename that may have been retrained since.
`UnderfitLoraCheckpoint.fromFile` computes that digest from a local file, which assumes Field and
the worker share a filesystem. [`UnderfitLoraCheckpoint`](audio-ai.md#underfitoperations-kt-underfitloracheckpoint)'s own `init` block checks what it can
before a request exists: the path stays inside the root and ends in `.safetensors`, the digest is
exactly 64 lowercase hex digits, strength is finite and non-negative, and the LoRA's denoising
interval satisfies
`0 <= intervalMin <= intervalMax <= 1`. [`UnderfitGenerationControls`](audio-ai.md#underfitoperations-kt-underfitgenerationcontrols) validates its sampling knobs
the same way, independently of any one request.
